items.title: [Perspectives] Horology and the heart
items.summary: At the turn of the 17th century, the Venetian physician Santorio Santorio (1561–1636) described an instrument that rendered the pulse measurable. items.title: Effects of fentanyl on diaphragm muscle force in patients undergoing knee arthroplasty: quantifying regression to the mean in diaphragm shear wave elastography. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 858–67
items.summary: Gransee and colleagues1 reported a demanding trial with an unusually practical protocol: diaphragm shear wave elastography across graded inspiratory loading, completed preoperatively in under 30 min without disrupting anaesthetic workflow. Among their secondary findings, the authors describe a negative association between the pre-fentanyl Young’s modulus range (E range) and the fentanyl-induced change in that range (ΔE range; P<0.001; r2=0.184; their Fig. 3b), advanced in the Discussion as the basis of a candidate biomarker of opioid susceptibility.

items.title: Inflammasome–caspase-1 activation is associated with infections in systemic inflammatory response syndrome after cardiac surgery: a prospective translational study
items.summary: Cardiac surgery triggers the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), characterised by a dysregulated immune response involving concurrent pro- and anti-inflammatory activation. Postoperative immunosuppression increases susceptibility to postoperative infections, prolonged hospitalisation, and mortality. After burns and stroke, circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) initiates immune dysregulation via inflammasome activation. Whether this mechanism similarly contributes to SIRS-associated immunosuppression after cardiac surgery is unknown.
